title: Exploring Cultural Variations in Moral Judgments with Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the alignment of Large Language Models' moral justifiability scores with human survey data from the World Values Survey (WVS) and Pew Global Attitudes Survey (PEW). It specifically probes the models on ethical topics like divorce, euthanasia, homosexuality, and alcohol consumption, where moral stances are often shaped by religious traditions, to assess cultural and moral variations.
base_benchmarks: Pew Research Center's Global Attitudes Survey (PEW)
findings: LLMs exhibit a significant W.E.I.R.D. (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) bias. Their moral judgments align poorly with those from non-Western regions like the Middle East/North Africa (MENA) and Sub-Saharan Africa. This misalignment is especially pronounced on topics heavily influenced by religious and cultural values, such as homosexuality and alcohol consumption, suggesting models fail to capture diverse moral norms rooted in different traditions. The paper also cites prior research indicating that GPT-3 associated Muslims with violence more frequently than Christians.
